Q1: Chlorotrifluoromethane has an expanded perspective on its environmental hazards (Tier 2) and is considered a low/moderate endocrine disruptor (Tier 3). However, its carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, inhalation, oral, dermal, and organ/systemic hazards are all data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: This chemical does not appear on any known lists of concern or low hazard. Given the high number of data-deficient hazard classifications, its absence from lists of concern may reflect a lack of study rather than confirmed safety.
Q3: While Chlorotrifluoromethane has a defined structure and a significant number of scientific literature references (3580), its hazard profile is not fully characterized. This is evidenced by the absence of rigorous EPA evaluations (IRIS/PPRTV), only 6 toxicity records, and numerous data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard classifications.
